body:
Adds `at_maximum` / `at_minimum`, which return a coordinate (or another field, interpolated to the extremum's location) where a field is extreme. The search runs on the device; only the index and the requested values come back to the host.

```julia
T = model.tracers.T
z_warmest = at_maximum(T, :z)
x, y, z = at_minimum(T, (:x, :y, :z))
w_at_peak = at_maximum(abs, T, model.velocities.w)   # w interpolated to T's location
z_masked = at_maximum(T, :z; condition = (i, j, k, grid, T) -> k > 2)
```

Also:
- `findmax(f, c)` / `findmin(f, c)` now work on fields, like Base.
- `locate_extremum` no longer relies on `operand === c`, which returns `false` for windowed fields on Julia 1.13 once the field crosses a function boundary, so the search read outside the window.
  This looks like a Julia bug; we still need a minimal reproducer (without Oceananigans) to report upstream.

title: Add at_maximum and at_minimum to locate coordinates of extrema

body:
at the moment, in main, we are limited to having `Nsteps < grid_size` when using extended halos (i.e. in distributed runs) because we compute the barotropic mode in the halos. 

This PR relaxes this requirement by filling the halos only when we need if we have `Nsteps > grid_size` (i.e. take the example that `Nsteps = 1.8grid_size`, then during the substepping we will need to fill the halos once when we reach `substep_index = grid_size`.

It will help reducing the impact of #6294, given that that case requires 2 halos per substep instead of 1.

body:
Time-stepping a `HydrostaticFreeSurfaceModel` with a `SplitExplicitFreeSurface` and a `DateTime` (or `TimeDate`) clock throws

```
MethodError: no method matching +(::DateTime, ::Float64)
```

in `step_free_surface!`. #5982 (substep clock) and #6151 (FieldTimeSeries window spanning the substeps) add `n * Δτᴮ` to `clock.time` directly. This PR uses `add_time_interval` instead, as schedules and the checkpointer already do.

The existing DateTime forcing test only used the default free surface, which is `ImplicitFreeSurface` on its 1×1×1 regular grid. It now also runs with `SplitExplicitFreeSurface(substeps=4)`. Without the fix, those 16 new cases error; with it, all 135 pass.

Found while moving NumericalEarth.jl to `DateTime` clocks: every realistic `ocean_simulation` uses a split-explicit free surface.
